adminHelp.startTitle: A safe way to use this page
adminHelp.sectionsCopy: Each topic below explains what the visible area controls, what an operator can do there, and what to check before changing anything.
adminHelp.roleBoundary: Your role determines which controls are shown and which changes Core will accept. A missing button may mean read-only access, not a broken page.
adminHelp.sourceBoundary: The values shown after a successful refresh come from Core. After a conflict, timeout, or uncertain save, refresh the authoritative state before trying another mutation.
adminHelp.unavailableCopy: This route is not in the current bounded help catalogue. Do not make a change until its operator guide is added and reviewed.

overview.title: Overview help
overview.summary: This is the operations starting point. It combines a current community snapshot with shortcuts and the newest administrator activity so a new operator can decide where attention is needed without changing any member data.

steps.1: Read the snapshot first and look for an unexpected change in registrations, avatar coverage, demo profiles, campaigns or active administrators.
steps.2: Open the focused module for the task you actually need; the overview itself is informational.
steps.3: Use Recent audit to confirm that an important change was recorded and to see who made it.

metrics.title: Community snapshot
metrics.purpose: The six cards summarize registered members, the last seven days of registrations, isolated demo profiles, active People campaigns, active administrators and avatar coverage.

actions.1: Compare the counts with the expected operating state and use them as navigation clues.
actions.2: Open Registered users or People hero when a number needs investigation; these cards do not edit the underlying records.

metrics.guidance: The values are live counts, not historical charts. Demo profiles are intentionally isolated and should never be interpreted as ordinary community growth.

quickActions.title: Quick actions
quickActions.purpose: These links take you to the most common support and content areas: registered members, the Discover hero carousel and allow-listed product configuration.

actions.1: Go straight to the relevant workspace without searching the long navigation menu.
actions.2: Return here after the task if you want a fresh operational snapshot.

quickActions.guidance: A shortcut grants no extra permission. The destination page and Core still enforce your administrator role.

recentAudit.title: Recent administrator activity
recentAudit.purpose: This feed shows the newest server-authored audit events with actor, action, target and time, giving a quick answer to what changed most recently.

actions.1: Review the latest five events for unexpected or duplicate operations.
actions.2: Open the full Audit log when you need filters, older events or safe event details.

recentAudit.guidance: An empty feed means no rows were returned; it is not permission to repeat an uncertain mutation. Refresh or inspect the full audit log first.

users.title: Registered users help
users.summary: This page is the member support directory. It helps operators find an account, distinguish regular and demo identities, understand the current membership result and open the full account workspace.

steps.1: Search with the narrowest reliable identifier, preferably UID or exact email, and confirm the displayed identity before acting.
steps.2: Read account type, location, membership lifecycle and source together; no single badge tells the whole account story.
steps.3: Open the member detail page for moderation, photos, profile data or membership operations.

filters.title: Search and account filters
filters.purpose: Search accepts a name, email, UID or username. Account type separates regular members from the isolated demo realm, and the avatar switch limits results to profiles with a picture.

actions.1: Combine search, account type and avatar state, then apply the filter.
actions.2: Reset all criteria when a known member is not found, and use pagination for broader result sets.

filters.guidance: Always verify UID and contact data in the result row. Similar display names are not enough to identify the correct member.

membershipSummary.title: Membership summary
membershipSummary.purpose: Each row separates tier, lifecycle, effective expiry, contributing sources and first known source date so support does not confuse a PLUS badge with verified billing evidence.

actions.1: Check whether access is currently effective and whether it comes from Store evidence, an administrator grant or another normalized source.
actions.2: Open the member detail for full evidence, grant history and safe membership controls.

membershipSummary.guidance: Unavailable or ambiguous evidence must not be turned into a guessed FREE or PLUS answer. Treat the Core projection as authoritative.

results.title: Member results and demo visibility
results.purpose: The table shows identity, contact, approximate location, registration time, account type, membership and the explicit permission that lets an approved regular account see demo profiles.

actions.1: Open the full account workspace from the row.
actions.2: Grant or revoke demo visibility only for an approved support or review purpose when the control is available.
actions.3: Move between server-paged results without changing the active filters.

results.guidance: Demo visibility does not convert an account into a demo identity and never merges the two realms. Record the operational reason outside this list when your procedure requires one.

userDetail.title: Member account help
userDetail.summary: This is the complete support workspace for one confirmed UID. It joins authoritative account facts with photo operations, effective membership, moderation, a time-bounded product popup, privacy-safe outbound messaging, boolean-only push-channel presence, public profile text and structured profile answers.

steps.1: Confirm the UID, display name and account state at the top before touching any control.
steps.2: Use the narrowest section for the requested task and read warnings or previews before saving.
steps.3: After a write, wait for the refreshed Core state and confirm the expected audit or history row.

identity.title: Member identity header
identity.purpose: The header anchors every operation to the selected UID and shows the current display identity and accepted avatar.

actions.1: Compare UID, display name, username or codename with the support request.
actions.2: Return to Registered users immediately if the identity does not match.

identity.guidance: Never rely on the avatar or display name alone; both can change and can be shared by different accounts.

albums.title: All profile albums
albums.purpose: This area exposes public, private and custom albums for authorized support, including image replacement, crop correction, main-photo selection and removal.

actions.1: Inspect the original image and its album scope before editing or deleting it.
actions.2: Replace or re-crop an image when the content is acceptable but presentation is wrong.
actions.3: Choose the accepted main photo or remove a specific image when policy and the support case justify it.

albums.guidance: Private album visibility in Webadmin is privileged support access. Do not copy, download or expose it beyond the case, and remember that deletion affects the member immediately.

membership.title: Effective membership
membership.purpose: This panel explains what the member can use now, public badge visibility, verified Store evidence and any time-bounded administrator grant.

actions.1: Review effective capabilities and the independent subscriber-badge result.
actions.2: Preview and issue or extend a PLUS grant when policy permits.
actions.3: For owner-only shortening or revocation, inspect overlap warnings and membership history first.

membership.guidance: An administrator grant never records payment and does not pause, cancel or extend Apple or Google billing. Avoid creating overlapping access unless the support decision explicitly requires it.

moderation.title: Moderation and access controls
moderation.purpose: The moderation panel manages temporary suspension, permanent ban, IP blocks, forced logout and the member-specific Footprint allowance.

actions.1: Apply or replace a suspension with a bounded duration and auditable reason.
actions.2: Ban or unban only after confirming the permanent account effect; manage IP blocks separately.
actions.3: Force logout for session containment, or set a daily Footprint override without changing the global default.

moderation.guidance: Suspension and ban hide the profile and conversations and terminate sessions. An IP block can affect other people sharing that address, while forced logout alone does not prevent signing back in.

productPopup.title: Per-member product popup
productPopup.purpose: This editor reads, previews, creates, replaces or clears the one time-bounded in-app product/support message assigned to this UID.

actions.1: Read the current Core-authored status, exact expiry and resource revision before drafting a replacement.
actions.2: Validate the normalized member preview, then confirm the exact content and expiry against the observed revision.
actions.3: After an uncertain response, reconcile authoritative state or retry only the saved request with its original identity.

productPopup.guidance: A product popup is not a push, support reply, moderation penalty or permanent gate. Never bypass its 30-day maximum, and never start a competing mutation while a durable request is unresolved.

outboundAvailability.title: Outbound channel availability
outboundAvailability.purpose: The availability cards distinguish available, absent, opted-out, ineligible and not-yet-migrated states without exposing a destination or push registration.

actions.1: Read each channel independently and treat the displayed state as Core's current policy result.
actions.2: Stop if any row is missing or malformed; never turn a failed availability read into an absent channel.

outboundAvailability.guidance: Availability means only that Core can currently resolve an eligible route. It does not prove delivery, reveal a provider, or override the member's preference.

outboundPreview.title: Recipient preview and capacity
outboundPreview.purpose: The preview binds the operator to an exact explicit UID list, shows safe display identity and reports current rolling all-channel and SMS-plus-push capacity.

actions.1: Confirm the UID and display identity before drafting any member-facing content.
actions.2: Check the selected channel, recipient count, remaining capacity and five-minute preview expiry together.
actions.3: Read a fresh preview if identity, availability, capacity or expiry changes.

outboundPreview.guidance: A preview reserves no capacity and guarantees no future delivery. Version 1 accepts only 1 to 100 explicit unique UIDs, never a query, cohort, place, event or campaign selector.

outboundContent.title: Template or custom content
outboundContent.purpose: The composer sends either one exact canonical template revision or bounded custom content with the template reference deliberately removed.

actions.1: Use Exact template when the immutable stored wording is appropriate and verify its observed revision.
actions.2: Switch explicitly to Custom content before changing any subject or body, then validate the channel-specific bounds.
actions.3: Inspect canonical email only inside the sandbox; custom email source remains inert until Core sanitizes it.

outboundContent.guidance: There is no variable substitution, attachment, arbitrary deep link, schedule or provider choice. Editing a template for one send must never retain template attribution.

outboundConfirmation.title: Confirmation, partial choice and audit
outboundConfirmation.purpose: The final review joins the exact recipient count, selected channel, content source, current availability, explicit partial-send behavior and factual internal reason.

actions.1: Enter a bounded operational reason that contains no unnecessary private information.
actions.2: Leave partial sending off unless the reviewed multi-member operation may legitimately skip unavailable recipients.
actions.3: Confirm only after the displayed recipient, content and preview still match the intended gesture.

outboundConfirmation.guidance: Partial sending never bypasses rate limits: if the full planned dispatch exceeds rolling capacity, nobody is selected. Core records audit intent before reservation or provider-visible work.

outboundResults.title: Send result and uncertain recovery
outboundResults.purpose: One closed outcome per UID distinguishes provider-accepted sent, durably queued, policy-skipped and terminally failed initial states without raw diagnostics.

actions.1: Treat Queued as durable acceptance for later work, not as proof of delivery.
actions.2: After a timeout, malformed response or in-progress result, preserve and retry only the exact saved request identity and material.
actions.3: Use authoritative history to observe later state changes instead of manufacturing another send.

outboundResults.guidance: Never mint a second request ID after uncertainty. An expired preview or rate-limit refusal ends that gesture and requires a fresh preview plus a new request identity.

outboundHistory.title: Bounded delivery history
outboundHistory.purpose: History rows show current aggregate status, immutable bounded subject and body excerpt, actor and times, template provenance and a content hash for one UID.

actions.1: Select a row to read its one UID-bound full canonical body and verify that its metadata matches the list snapshot.
actions.2: Use current history for queued, retrying, partially sent, failed, skipped or suppressed state after the initial receipt.
actions.3: Restart from the first page when Core rejects a stale history cursor.

outboundHistory.guidance: Partially sent is an aggregate push state and deliberately does not reveal which provider accepted or failed. One malformed stored row invalidates the complete read; it is never skipped into a false empty list.

outboundPrivacy.title: Messaging permissions and privacy
outboundPrivacy.purpose: History read, outbound send, canned-template read and canned-template edit are independent Core capabilities that the browser must never derive from an administrator role name.

actions.1: Use read-only history access for investigation without assuming permission to preview or send.
actions.2: Use a stored template only when the separate template-read capability is present; sending never grants template editing.
actions.3: Keep member destinations and transport diagnostics outside screenshots, notes and copied case material.

outboundPrivacy.guidance: Email addresses, phone numbers, tokens, device values, provider identifiers, credentials, provider responses and raw errors are intentionally unavailable in preview, results, history, audit and browser state.

pushChannels.title: Member push-channel presence
pushChannels.purpose: This read-only panel reports whether Core can currently resolve at least one usable FCM registration and at least one usable OneSignal registration for this UID.

actions.1: Read each provider independently; a member can have neither, one or both registrations.
actions.2: Compare presence with the global delivery mode when investigating why a provider is or is not eligible for a push.

pushChannels.guidance: Presence is not proof that a notification was sent or delivered. The console never exposes raw registrations, hashes, device identifiers, provider errors or credentials.

verificationGrant.title: Verification level and team grant
verificationGrant.purpose: This panel separates method statuses, derived or imported verification, the effective level and any upward-only team grant for the confirmed member.

actions.1: Read the applied region, method statuses, provenance and evaluated expiry before considering a grant.
actions.2: Preview Light or Strong with a private bounded reason and optional expiry, then review the privacy-safe pink-seal consequence.
actions.3: Remove only the team grant when appropriate; genuine Video selfie, Persona and imported verification remain unchanged.

verificationGrant.guidance: Strong changes internal access, but other members see only the same pink verified seal with no tier disclosure. This panel cannot override the member's badge-visibility preference or revoke genuine verification.

adminGrantedVerification.title: Admin-granted verification authority
adminGrantedVerification.purpose: This distinct panel shows the retained evidence-free admin seal, its safe reason witness, the member's currently enabled grant methods and the final effective verification without presenting a fake provider result.

actions.1: Confirm the UID, exact revision, current enabled methods and whether another genuine or imported authority already wins.
actions.2: Choose only a currently enabled method, enter the bounded internal reason and explicitly confirm before granting.
actions.3: Revoke the active admin grant when required, even if its method was disabled later, then verify the authoritative returned state.

adminGrantedVerification.guidance: A provider-free grant is audited authority, not Persona, Video selfie or manual-review evidence. Never create a second request ID after an uncertain response; retry the exact saved command.

audienceVisibility.title: Who can see my profile
audienceVisibility.purpose: This read-only panel reports the member's canonical audience-visibility gender, who their profile is visible to, the one protected group Core derives from that pair together with its legacy segment, and the revision those three were read at.

actions.1: Read the gender, the visibility value and the derived group together; an unresolved gender means Core can derive no group, not that the member was taken out of one.
actions.2: Note the visibility revision before asking the Audience visibility workspace to change anything, because every write there is checked against it.
actions.3: Use Retry authoritative read when the panel reports a decoding error, and never treat a refused or undecodable read as an absent or default audience.

audienceVisibility.guidance: The panel is present only for an operator Core projects the audience-visibility member read to, so a colleague may genuinely not see it on the same member. It is a view, not an editor: groups, retirement and intents are configured on Audience visibility, and a nonbinary member is visible to everyone because that is the only protected group the contract defines for them.

profileCopy.title: Public profile texts
profileCopy.purpose: Operators can correct the member's headline and About text when handling support or accepted-content moderation.

actions.1: Edit only the text that is in scope for the case.
actions.2: Save the accepted replacement and verify the refreshed value.

profileCopy.guidance: Saving marks this copy as accepted content. Preserve the member's voice and do not rewrite unrelated text.

profileAnswers.title: Identity and structured profile answers
profileAnswers.purpose: This editor shows the current signup identity axes and the profile-field answers the member is eligible to hold, organized by the configured profile sections.

actions.1: Correct identity fields only when the request and policy establish the intended values.
actions.2: Add, replace or clear selectable profile answers and save against the current revision.
actions.3: Review unassigned or archived answers without silently deleting preserved history.

profileAnswers.guidance: Identity values influence discovery audiences and dynamic groups. A stale revision or changed eligibility must be refreshed, never merged optimistically in the browser.

accountFacts.title: Account facts
accountFacts.purpose: Read-only account metadata provides contact, registration and activity context for support.

actions.1: Use these facts to verify the account and understand its age or recent activity.
actions.2: Cross-check them with the case instead of treating them as editable profile content.

accountFacts.guidance: These are support projections, not proof of identity. Sensitive fields not required by this screen are deliberately omitted.

locationFacts.title: Location facts
locationFacts.purpose: The current public location and hometown labels help explain discovery or profile context without exposing raw coordinates.

actions.1: Compare the displayed city or region with the member's reported issue.
actions.2: Use Profile location configuration for policy questions, not this read-only summary.

locationFacts.guidance: The page intentionally does not project coordinates. Do not infer an exact location from these labels.

profileFacts.title: Profile facts
profileFacts.purpose: This read-only summary repeats the currently stored headline, About text and height for quick support review.

actions.1: Confirm that recent edits converged to the expected values.
actions.2: Use the dedicated editors above when a correction is authorized.

profileFacts.guidance: A blank value is a real absence, not a reason to invent replacement content for the member.

gallery.title: Gallery and moderation state
gallery.purpose: The summary gallery shows active, pending or rejected image status and links pending items to the human moderation queue.

actions.1: Open an image for inspection in a separate tab.
actions.2: Follow a pending image to Photo moderation for an explicit decision.

gallery.guidance: Use the album workspace above for member-owned image mutations. This gallery is a status view and must not be mistaken for proof that a pending image is public.

interests.title: Interests
interests.purpose: The tag list shows the member's stored profile interests in a compact support-readable form.

actions.1: Use the values to understand profile presentation or a reported matching issue.
actions.2: Manage the available catalog in Profile tag catalogs rather than editing this read-only list.

interests.guidance: Stored selections can survive catalog archival so members can remove retired values. Their presence here does not mean the item is still selectable.

membership.title: Membership plans help
membership.summary: This workspace defines the FREE and PLUS capability model, quotas and operator grant presets. It prepares server-owned membership behavior; deployment switches and Store product identities remain outside ordinary editing.

steps.1: Review release gates and Core validation before editing benefits or quotas.
steps.2: Use the member and grant previews to read the complete effect of the draft.
steps.3: Save only a validated revision, then verify readiness separately from live enforcement.

rollout.title: Release gates
rollout.purpose: Read-only rollout switches explain whether membership enforcement is still in shadow mode or permitted to affect live access.

actions.1: Confirm which environment gates are active before interpreting a saved draft as live behavior.
actions.2: Use the warnings to identify missing client, provider or server dependencies.

rollout.guidance: Saving configuration does not enable enforcement. Rollout gates are deployment-owned and must never be toggled merely to make this page appear complete.

benefits.title: Tier capabilities
benefits.purpose: Capabilities state whether each named feature is available to FREE and PLUS members, with Core remaining the final authority.

actions.1: Compare the two tiers for every benefit and change only reviewed product policy.
actions.2: Read the explanation below each capability to understand the member-visible effect.

benefits.guidance: A stale client may still show old copy, but it cannot overrule Core. Coordinate capability changes with every supported client.

limits.title: Quotas and resource limits
limits.purpose: Every quota is explicit per tier: disabled, finite or unlimited, with daily counters using UTC and concurrent limits counting active resources.

actions.1: Choose the mode for each tier and enter a bounded number only for finite limits.
actions.2: Review every validation error before saving.

limits.guidance: Lower limits can affect members immediately when enforcement is live. Understand whether a rule is daily or concurrent before changing its value.

preview.title: Member and grant previews
preview.purpose: The preview translates the draft into member-facing entitlements and shows the time-bounded administrator grant presets available on member accounts.

actions.1: Switch preview tiers to verify that benefits and limits read as intended.
actions.2: Review preset duration and result before operators rely on it for support grants.

preview.guidance: The preview includes unsaved draft values and is not a promise that rollout gates are enabled. Grant presets never represent a Store purchase.

products.title: Store product allow-list
products.purpose: This read-only inventory names the Apple and Google products Core recognizes as possible membership evidence.

actions.1: Confirm the expected products exist for each platform.
actions.2: Use readiness warnings to identify provider provisioning still outside Webadmin.

products.guidance: A listed product is not proof that receipt verification, notifications or signed-device purchase evidence are complete. Product identities cannot be created here.

readiness.title: Configuration readiness
readiness.purpose: The readiness marker records that values, copy, migrations and compatibility have been reviewed for this revision.

actions.1: Mark ready only after validation and cross-client review are complete.
actions.2: Save the marker with the same optimistic revision as the rest of the configuration.

readiness.guidance: Ready is an operator assertion, not the enforcement switch. External provider and physical-device gates may still block release.

photoModeration.title: Profile photo moderation help
photoModeration.summary: This queue is the human decision point for profile and album images held by automated SafeSearch or the legacy moderation path before they are allowed to become public.

steps.1: Choose the correct profile, private-album or public-album queue and inspect the original image.
steps.2: Read scan likelihoods as context, then make an independent human policy decision.
steps.3: Approve, reject or correct the image once, and confirm that it leaves the pending queue.

queueScopes.title: Queue scope
queueScopes.purpose: Tabs separate main profile pictures, private-album pictures and public-album pictures because visibility and support context differ.

actions.1: Switch scopes and refresh to load the latest bounded queue.
actions.2: Use the displayed count to understand only the currently selected scope.

queueScopes.guidance: Private-album review is privileged access. Do not treat a private image as public content or reuse it outside the moderation case.

reviewCards.title: Image review cards
reviewCards.purpose: Each card joins the original image, member and album context, creation time, automated likelihoods and the reasons it needs review.

actions.1: Open the original at full size and, when necessary, open the member account for surrounding context.
actions.2: Use Edit or square crop to correct presentation when the content itself is acceptable.

reviewCards.guidance: Automated labels support the review; they do not decide it. Verify the actual image and current policy before pressing a terminal action.

approve.title: Approve an image
approve.purpose: Approval accepts the pending media for its intended profile or album scope and removes it from the human queue.

actions.1: Approve only after confirming both content safety and the correct owning member.
actions.2: Wait for the queue refresh and verify the card no longer appears as pending.

approve.guidance: Approval can make profile media visible immediately. Do not approve simply because the automated scan says safe.

reject.title: Reject an image
reject.purpose: Rejection records that the image must not enter the intended visible media scope.

actions.1: Reject when the image violates the applicable content or presentation policy.
actions.2: Confirm the completed decision before moving to the next card.

reject.guidance: Rejection affects member content. Make sure a simple crop or correction would not be the more proportionate action.

reportedContentQueue.title: Reported-content queue help
reportedContentQueue.summary: This is the global report triage queue for safe user/profile and chat-message projections. It separates pending work from resolved history, preserves authoritative pagination and never treats a malformed read as proof that no reports exist.

steps.1: Choose the pending or resolved status and target type that matches your assigned moderation work.
steps.2: Open one report, identify the reporter and subject, and read only the bounded material Core deliberately projects.
steps.3: Use the detail page for any decision, then verify the authoritative status before continuing to another report.

filters.title: Status and target filters
filters.purpose: The two closed filters separate pending, confirmed and rejected reports and distinguish profile targets from chat-message targets.

actions.1: Select the narrowest status and target combination relevant to the current assignment.
actions.2: Refresh the first page after changing filters or when another moderator may have acted.

filters.guidance: An empty result proves only that the selected normalized filter is empty. It is never evidence that the whole moderation history is empty.

queue.title: Authoritative report rows
queue.purpose: Each row identifies the reporter, reported member, target kind, member reason, current report state and creation time without returning whole user or chat documents.

actions.1: Use the visible report ID and member identities to open the intended detail record.
actions.2: Prioritize pending rows in their oldest-first order and avoid deciding from list metadata.

queue.guidance: A report indicates an allegation, not a proven violation. Open the detail and evaluate the projected context before recording an outcome.

safeProjection.title: Safe projected material
safeProjection.purpose: Core limits queue content to plain text, bounded labels and safe member identifiers while withholding contacts, coordinates, private URLs and raw evidence.

actions.1: Read the projected reason and target kind as context, not as unrestricted account evidence.
actions.2: Stop and report a load failure if any row is incomplete instead of working around it.

safeProjection.guidance: Do not seek direct storage paths or copy report material into external tickets. Restricted evidence requires a separately contracted bridge.

capabilities.title: Read and decision capabilities
capabilities.purpose: The queue displays Core-authored capabilities independently from the role label, so the console never invents decision authority for a viewer or future narrower role.

actions.1: Use read-only access for triage and escalation without attempting a terminal report decision.
actions.2: Expect decision controls only when Core explicitly returns the report-decision capability.

capabilities.guidance: A role name is descriptive, not authorization evidence. Core rechecks the decision capability again at mutation time.

pagination.title: Cursor pagination
pagination.purpose: Load-more uses an opaque cursor bound to the current filters and preserves unique stable report IDs across every accepted page.

actions.1: Load subsequent pages without changing either filter while the cursor remains active.
actions.2: Restart from the first page when Core reports a stale or invalid cursor.

pagination.guidance: Never interpret or manufacture a cursor. A duplicate, malformed or out-of-order page fails closed instead of extending a partial queue.

reportedContentDetail.title: Reported-content detail help
reportedContentDetail.summary: This workspace shows one exact report and permits one revision-bound confirm or reject decision. It preserves a caller-minted request ID across uncertain responses, adopts conflicts without merging, and deliberately performs no automatic ban or content deletion.

steps.1: Confirm the report ID, revision, reporter and reported member before interpreting the bounded target material.
steps.2: If Core grants decision capability, select confirm or reject and write a factual internal reason before reviewing the confirmation.
steps.3: After any uncertain response, retry the saved request unchanged until Core returns replay, convergence or a terminal conflict.

identities.title: Reporter and reported member
identities.purpose: The identity cards expose only UID, display name and username for the two people needed to understand and investigate this report.

actions.1: Verify that both identity cards correspond to the report you intended to review.
actions.2: Open a member profile only when additional authorized support context is necessary.

identities.guidance: The projection intentionally omits contact, social-provider, birthday, relationship and location details. Do not infer missing identity data.

reportedMaterial.title: Bounded reported material
reportedMaterial.purpose: Profile reports carry a short plain-text summary; chat reports carry bounded message text or an explicit removed/unavailable state plus restricted-evidence presence only.

actions.1: Read the availability marker before interpreting an empty chat-message text value.
actions.2: Treat the restricted-evidence badge as a boundary marker, not as permission to retrieve files.

reportedMaterial.guidance: Direct storage paths, private URLs and unrestricted conversations are outside this contract. Never replace unavailable evidence with guesses.

decision.title: Confirm or reject the report
decision.purpose: A decision changes only the pending report to confirmed or rejected at the exact displayed revision and records a bounded operator reason.

actions.1: Confirm only when the projected context supports that the member's report is valid.
actions.2: Reject when the report is not confirmed, and explain that conclusion factually without unnecessary private data.

decision.guidance: This decision never bans a user, suspends an account or deletes content. Use separate explicit audited tools if later policy action is required.

conflictRetry.title: Conflict and uncertain-response recovery
conflictRetry.purpose: The page stores one request ID, expected revision, action and reason before mutation so a timeout or lost response cannot become a second logical decision.

actions.1: Use Retry saved request whenever the pending-request banner remains visible.
actions.2: On a revision conflict, review the adopted Core row instead of merging it with the old draft.

conflictRetry.guidance: Do not clear the pending identity or mint another UUID after a network, timeout, service or in-progress response. Exact replay is the recovery path.

resolution.title: Authoritative resolution
resolution.purpose: Resolved reports show the decision, internal reason, deciding administrator and timestamp returned by Core with the incremented revision.

actions.1: Verify that the returned decision and reason match the confirmed operator gesture.
actions.2: Use the resolution as immutable history and do not attempt to submit another decision.

resolution.guidance: A replayed success is the original completion, not a second change. Resolved reports remain visible for accountable moderation history.

boundaries.title: Authorization and evidence boundaries
boundaries.purpose: Core authors read/decide capabilities, overwrites administrator identity, validates every mutation and persists audit intent before the report state can change.

actions.1: Stop when decision capability is absent and escalate through the approved operational path.
actions.2: Keep operator reasons factual and exclude private evidence, contact data and direct storage references.

boundaries.guidance: The browser never calls Core directly and cannot widen its own role. An audit-write refusal leaves the report untouched and retains the same retry identity.

profileVerificationQueue.title: Profile verification queue help
profileVerificationQueue.summary: This page lists members who submitted a private video selfie for manual comparison with their current accepted main photo. Queue rows contain metadata; private evidence opens only inside a claimed case.

steps.1: Filter to the status you are assigned to handle and open one case at a time.
steps.2: Check age, avatar-change and lease metadata before requesting evidence.
steps.3: Complete the review in the case page, where every sensitive read and decision is audited.

statusFilter.title: Status filter
statusFilter.purpose: The filter separates pending, in-review, approved, denied and other supported verification lifecycle states.

actions.1: Select the status relevant to your queue assignment.
actions.2: Refresh when another reviewer or the avatar reconciler may have changed state.

statusFilter.guidance: A proven empty result applies only to the active filter. It does not mean no verification history exists.

caseQueue.title: Verification cases
caseQueue.purpose: Rows identify the member, current status, revision, submission age and review context without streaming biometric evidence into the list.

actions.1: Open the intended case and avoid parallel reviews of the same member.
actions.2: Use visible state and timing to prioritize pending work.

caseQueue.guidance: Metadata access does not grant evidence access. Editors and owners must still claim and explicitly open private files.

caseMetadata.title: Case and avatar context
caseMetadata.purpose: Queue metadata helps spot stale submissions, current-avatar changes and cases already being handled.

actions.1: Notice avatar warnings and reviewer ownership before opening a case.
actions.2: Let the case detail and Core resolve revision or lifecycle conflicts.

caseMetadata.guidance: Never approve from list metadata. The decision requires comparison of the issued challenge video with the exact current accepted avatar.

configurationLink.title: Verification flow configuration
configurationLink.purpose: The configuration shortcut leads to the separate bilingual member flow, consent copy, challenge prompts and status colors.

actions.1: Open configuration when the issue concerns what members see or consent to, not an individual case.
actions.2: Return to the queue for case handling.

configurationLink.guidance: Changing flow copy does not decide existing cases and must not weaken privacy or consent requirements.

profileVerificationDetail.title: Verification case help
profileVerificationDetail.summary: This is the restricted manual-review workspace for one profile-video case. It separates current member facts, immutable case-time context, reviewer ownership, private evidence, decision controls and append-only history.

steps.1: Confirm the member, case revision and avatar warnings, then claim the reviewer lease.
steps.2: Open evidence only for this review and compare the exact challenge sequence with the current accepted avatar.
steps.3: Record one supported decision and verify the resulting history event before leaving.

member.title: Current member data
member.purpose: This section shows the authoritative current profile and avatar state used to detect a submission that became stale after an avatar change.

actions.1: Compare the current avatar hash and member facts with the immutable case context.
actions.2: Stop if the accepted avatar is missing or changed.

member.guidance: Core intentionally conflicts an approval against the wrong avatar. Do not work around an avatar-change warning.

case.title: Immutable review case
case.purpose: The case block records submission-time identity, avatar reference, status, revision and evidence availability.

actions.1: Read the case-time values before opening any media.
actions.2: Use the displayed revision for every claim or decision generated by the page.

case.guidance: A stale revision means another authoritative event occurred. Refresh instead of attempting to merge states.

lease.title: Reviewer lease
lease.purpose: A five-minute claim assigns active handling to one reviewer, while heartbeat and release manage that short ownership window.

actions.1: Claim the case before opening evidence or deciding it.
actions.2: Keep the lease alive while reviewing, and release it when abandoning the case.

lease.guidance: A lease reduces duplicate work but does not replace optimistic revisions. Another valid lifecycle change can still make the case stale.

evidence.title: Private comparison evidence
evidence.purpose: The protected video and avatar snapshot are closed by default and served through an authenticated, no-store, audited bridge.

actions.1: Open evidence only after claiming the case and only when needed for the decision.
actions.2: Review the video and accepted-avatar snapshot without downloading or redistributing them.

evidence.guidance: These files are sensitive biometric comparison material, not public URLs. Do not capture them in screenshots, tickets or audit notes.

challenge.title: Issued challenge sequence
challenge.purpose: The ordered prompts tell the reviewer which head turns and expression the member was asked to perform.

actions.1: Watch for every movement in the exact listed order.
actions.2: Use client timestamps only as diagnostic context.

challenge.guidance: The V1 flow records human-review evidence; it does not claim automated identity, document or liveness verification.

decisions.title: Approve, reject or request a new video
decisions.purpose: The supported decisions update the verification lifecycle for the exact current avatar and optionally retain a private reviewer note.

actions.1: Approve only when the video and current accepted avatar clearly show the same person and the movements are clear.
actions.2: Reject when the case fails policy, or request one replacement when a new usable capture is appropriate.
actions.3: Read the confirmation and submit only once.

decisions.guidance: A reviewer note is internal and bounded, but it should still contain no unnecessary sensitive description. The public badge is tied to the exact avatar hash.

history.title: Verification history
history.purpose: Append-only events explain consent, submission, avatar changes, reviewer activity, decisions and later lifecycle transitions.

actions.1: Confirm that your evidence read and decision produced the expected events.
actions.2: Use history to understand a re-review or replacement without overwriting earlier facts.

history.guidance: History is evidence, not an editable note pad. A missing expected event should be investigated before repeating any action.

verification.title: Verification settings help
verification.summary: This guarded workspace manages regional Verification policy, atomic bilingual gate copy, managed PNG assets, synthetic evaluation and upward-only team grants. Core remains the sole authorization and enforcement authority.

steps.1: Start with Scopes: confirm the current effective source, distinguish saved draft from live policy, and inspect every inherited field.
steps.2: Generate a fresh impact preview before a live operation, review its counts and activation guard, then type the exact phrase shown.
steps.3: Edit English and Hungarian copy as one pair, validate PNG assets locally, and run synthetic scenarios without entering a member UID.
steps.4: For every mutation, send one gesture only; after uncertainty, retain and retry the exact saved request or reconcile authoritative state.

overview.title: Verification policy workspace
overview.purpose: The six tabs expose the complete bounded Verification control plane only when Core's current action projection lists the console for this operator.

actions.1: Read the activation guard and import-health counts before preparing any live operation.
actions.2: Treat the all-None launch policy as inert; activation of a non-None requirement is a separate reviewed release operation.

overview.guidance: Visible controls do not grant authority. Core rechecks the current capability on every request, and a malformed response never becomes an empty or editable state.

methodsAndLevels.title: Methods and levels
methodsAndLevels.purpose: Verified Video contributes Light, verified Persona contributes Strong, and the effective level is the maximum of derived, valid imported and active granted authority.

actions.1: Confirm that one enabled method suppresses tier language and a Video-only Strong requirement clamps to Light.
actions.2: Confirm that both methods off clamps every effective requirement to None and emits no external seal.

methodsAndLevels.guidance: Disabling a method prevents new starts but does not rewrite an earned method result, import or team grant. Pending never contributes a level.

scopePrecedence.title: Scope precedence
scopePrecedence.purpose: Core resolves the member's current server-written city, then current country, registration or IP country, and finally global; each override field inherits independently.

actions.1: Inspect the exact source scope beside effective methods and every feature requirement.
actions.2: Use the simulator to verify city-to-country-to-global fallback without entering coordinates, IPs or a member identity.

scopePrecedence.guidance: Location scope is product personalization, not proof of identity, residency, fraud status or security. Webadmin never derives it from browser coordinates.

scopeEditing.title: Add and pause overrides
scopeEditing.purpose: A complete saved draft has no member effect until a separate live operation; country and city fields inherit exactly, while global forbids inheritance. New overrides remain draft-only until published.

actions.1: Use a closed ISO country or one current Core-proxied Places detail token; typed city text alone cannot create authority.
actions.2: Save the complete draft at the observed revision, then generate a new impact preview before publish, deactivate, tombstone or restore.
actions.3: For a draft-only publish, review the parent-derived effective-before values. Restoring its tombstone returns it to draft-only and still requires a separate publish.

scopeEditing.guidance: Only live policy affects members. Restore never publishes a draft. Global is always active and non-deletable; override removal is a retained tombstone, never a physical delete.

featureMatrix.title: Feature requirements
featureMatrix.purpose: The matrix contains all ten frozen feature keys exactly once and shows the live clamped tier from each field's exact inheritance source.

actions.1: Read the localized feature label and machine key before changing a complete draft cell.
actions.2: Check the configured and effective tier, especially Video-only Strong-to-Light and both-off-to-None clamps.

featureMatrix.guidance: Unknown, duplicate or missing keys are a contract mismatch, not optional rows. Draft edits never authorize a feature until a guarded live publication succeeds.

gateMessages.title: Bilingual gate messages
gateMessages.purpose: Five required default pairs and optional per-feature overrides store bounded plain-text English and Hungarian material atomically with semantic assets and safe actions.

actions.1: Edit both locales together and verify labels are present exactly when their action exists; URL actions accept bounded safe HTTPS only.
actions.2: Keep Pending information-only: it never unlocks, launch overdue copy starts at 30 minutes, and no timer turns it terminal automatically. Queue-average long copy is not available in v1.

gateMessages.guidance: Automatic actions are resolved by Core from current state. Copy cannot force a provider start, expose provider detail or create an authorization bypass.

badges.title: Verification badges
badges.purpose: The managed Light, Strong and Pending slots accept only square PNG input; other-member presentation always uses one pink seal regardless of earned tier.

actions.1: Choose a PNG of 16–2048 square pixels and no more than 2 MiB; Core performs bounded decode, metadata stripping and re-encoding.
actions.2: Remember that badge visibility changes presentation only; it never changes a method, level, feature decision or provider state.

badges.guidance: Other members receive at most the single pink seal when level, enabled-method and Privacy conditions all pass. They never receive Light or Strong.

simulator.title: Test a policy safely
simulator.purpose: Synthetic scope, method, provenance and badge-visibility inputs run Core's pure evaluator and return all ten feature decisions without touching a member.

actions.1: Exercise no-match, inherited, pending, rejected, imported, granted and both-off combinations before rollout.
actions.2: Compare the full Core-authored level, deterministic source, clamp, copy key and modal; never infer access from a partial row.

simulator.guidance: A simulator success is explanatory output, not an authorization token. It accepts no UID, evidence, provider payload or free-text location authority.

teamGrant.title: Team verification grant
teamGrant.purpose: The member-detail panel previews an upward-only Light or Strong grant; effective authority is max(derived, valid imported, active granted) at one Core time.

actions.1: Compare derived, imported and current grant authority, choose an optional future expiry, and preview at the observed grant revision.
actions.2: For Strong, acknowledge the fresh warning before saving; removal expires only the retained positive grant.

teamGrant.guidance: Expiry is strict at Core's captured time. Removal is not a negative revocation and cannot lower genuine Video, Persona or valid imported authority.

forcedWaitingRoom.title: Forced verification and Waiting Room
forcedWaitingRoom.purpose: Marks Persona or selfie-video verification as mandatory globally or per App Store storefront; gated members see the Waiting Room until one forced method is satisfied. The Waiting Room text and its optional help URL are edited here too.

actions.1: Set the global default first, then add a storefront override only where the rule differs; an override replaces the whole method set, so two switches off means not forced there.
actions.2: Edit the Waiting Room text in both languages, check the light and dark phone preview for the storefront, run the impact preview, and save at the shown revision.
actions.3: Set a Help URL per language when members should have somewhere to read more: an https address of at most 2048 bytes without credentials. The round “?” button appears in the Waiting Room only where an effective URL exists; a storefront override left blank inherits the global URL, and a blank global URL means no button.

forcedWaitingRoom.guidance: Seeded state forces nothing. Core evaluates the gate server-side with the member's last-seen storefront; a malformed stored document fails safe (nothing forced) while this tab reports it. The help URL is presentation only: it opens in an in-app browser over the Waiting Room and never lets a member past the gate. Switch forcing on only after the iOS build carrying the Waiting Room is live in the App Store: the gate applies to every app version, and an older app receives the refusal without a screen to show for it.

conflictsAndRetry.title: Conflicts and uncertain saves
conflictsAndRetry.purpose: Impact preview binds operation, scope, revisions, normalized result, method readiness and activation guard into one fingerprint and exact typed phrase.

actions.1: If covered state drifts or the preview becomes stale, discard it and generate a new preview before another apply request.
actions.2: After timeout, malformed response, 5xx or in-progress state, retain and reuse the exact session-stored request id and material.

conflictsAndRetry.guidance: Never duplicate the gesture or mint a second request id after uncertainty. Clear the saved pair only after validated convergence or a terminal input conflict.

privacyAndAudit.title: Privacy and audit boundaries
privacyAndAudit.purpose: Per-request capabilities, audit-before-domain ordering and minimal projections keep policy and support operations separate from provider or biometric evidence.

actions.1: Keep operator reasons, copy text and PNG bytes out of logs; receipts store bounded fingerprints and canonical safe results only.
actions.2: Verify that projections to other members contain only the allowed pink seal—never level, source, method, pending, rejected, grant or administrator detail.

privacyAndAudit.guidance: The page never exposes provider keys, inquiry ids, evidence, exact coordinates or IPs, private paths, member tier, raw receipts or administrator identity to public presentation.

persona.title: Persona operations help
persona.summary: This guarded workspace provides narrowly scoped member overrides and reports the current status of the Persona start-screen surface. Core authors readiness and capabilities; Webadmin keeps exact confirmations and durable receipt retry.

steps.1: Read the contract-readiness badges first; a dormant or missing action means stop, not permission to work around the gate.
steps.2: For a member operation, resolve the canonical UID and compare both UID and display name before selecting one action.
steps.3: Follow the start-screen panel shown on this page: a compiled-copy notice means there is no live editor to use; an intentionally restored editor carries its own revision and preview controls.
steps.4: After timeout, malformed response, 5xx or in-progress state, use only the exact session-stored retry; after a revision conflict, refresh authoritative state.

readiness.title: Contract and capabilities
readiness.purpose: The readiness panel proves the schema version, provider release state and whether Core granted this administrator read-only or write actions.

actions.1: Confirm that contract readiness is active before expecting any Persona proxy action to be reachable.
actions.2: Use only controls whose exact action appears in the current Core-authored capability list.

readiness.guidance: Role labels and visible buttons are not authority. A runtime readiness downgrade or removed action must close the corresponding control immediately.

memberLookup.title: Canonical member lookup
memberLookup.purpose: The lookup accepts one positive base-10 UID and stores only UID, display name and the shared Persona revision needed to anchor a confirmation and optimistic write.

actions.1: Enter the exact UID without a sign, decimal point or leading zero, then resolve it through the authenticated proxy.
actions.2: Compare the returned display name, UID and current revision with the support case before opening a confirmation.

memberLookup.guidance: The safe target projection deliberately omits provider attributes, inquiry identifiers, birth data and raw verification evidence. Never infer them from this card.

syntheticMarker.title: Synthetic marker controls
syntheticMarker.purpose: Apply marks an eligible member with an explicitly admin-created Persona state; revoke removes only that guarded synthetic state.

actions.1: Apply only for an approved operational purpose and state clearly that it is not provider-backed verification.
actions.2: Revoke only after confirming the target; let Core refuse real, provider-backed or force-promoted states.

syntheticMarker.guidance: Neither action verifies phone ownership. Core records audit intent before mutation, and the browser must never label a synthetic marker as a Persona provider check.

forceVerify.title: Avatar promotion override
forceVerify.purpose: The force operation copies the member's current durable avatar into the accepted Persona verification-image model and marks the member accepted.

actions.1: Read the high-impact confirmation naming the member and UID before promoting the current avatar.
actions.2: After success, verify that the canonical receipt advanced the displayed member revision; the returned relative path is validated and discarded.

forceVerify.guidance: This replaces verification evidence and is not a provider inquiry. Missing or non-durable avatars must remain Core refusals, never browser-side workarounds.

startConfig.title: Complete start-screen editor
startConfig.purpose: Eleven groups cover every contracted boolean, progress value, font size, URL, color, icon fallback and text field in the native pre-inquiry screen.

actions.1: Open only the group you need, edit bounded values, and inspect the normalized-change count.
actions.2: Discard the draft to restore the last complete Core object, or add a bounded private reason and confirm one partial patch at its exact revision.

startConfig.guidance: Sizes clamp to 8–80, progress remains any finite contracted number, and strings use their field caps. Unchanged defaults stay byte-preserved and are not silently rewritten.

preview.title: Normalized device preview
preview.purpose: The non-interactive phone frame renders the normalized draft's hierarchy, highlighted copy, benefit cards, trust content, action, safety card and skip state.

actions.1: Check content order, visibility switches, typography and contrast before opening the save confirmation.
actions.2: Verify every intended highlight marker and fallback icon behavior rather than relying on field names alone.

preview.guidance: The preview is an approximation, not an iOS screenshot. It loads images only from the Friending image host so an arbitrary configured host cannot track an administrator.

uncertainResponses.title: Receipt retry and conflicts
uncertainResponses.purpose: Every mutation stores its lowercase UUIDv4, action, target, expected revision, normalized material and private reason in sessionStorage before the first network byte is sent.

actions.1: After timeout, malformed response, 5xx or in-progress state, use Retry exact request; never mint a replacement UUID or edit its material.
actions.2: Clear the retained row only after a canonical success/replay, proven configuration convergence, or terminal conflict; refresh after stale revision.

uncertainResponses.guidance: Competing controls remain locked while a receipt is pending. Member revision alone cannot prove convergence, so an uncertain member mutation must obtain its canonical receipt by exact retry.

cannedTemplates.title: Message templates help
cannedTemplates.summary: This workspace manages only reusable email, SMS and push templates. Core owns capability checks, canonical email sanitization, revisions, receipts and audit intent; the console keeps channel content bounded, previews canonical output safely and never opens a delivery workflow.

steps.1: Choose one channel and use the internal-name filter to load a complete authoritative result.
steps.2: Select a stored template or start a new one, then review channel-specific limits and the normalized draft.
steps.3: Write an internal audit reason, open a fresh confirmation and submit one revisioned mutation.
steps.4: If a request becomes pending, keep controls locked and retry only the exact saved request identity until Core returns convergence or conflict.

channels.title: Email, SMS and push channels
channels.purpose: Each channel has an immutable format and exact subject/body rules: sanitized HTML email, subjectless plain SMS, or titled plain push.

actions.1: Choose the intended channel before creating a template.
actions.2: Treat moving content between channels as a separate create and separately confirmed delete.

channels.guidance: Channel rules are storage contracts, not presentation hints. The console never changes an existing template's channel or silently truncates content.

listSearch.title: Authoritative list and search
listSearch.purpose: The list binds every page and cursor to one channel, normalized name query and fixed page size, ordered by update time and stable identifier.

actions.1: Search only by the internal operator name and read the exact total returned by Core.
actions.2: Load subsequent pages with the issued cursor; restart from page one after a cursor refusal.

listSearch.guidance: A malformed stored row fails the whole read. Never interpret a parser error as an empty template library or skip an inconvenient row.

editor.title: Bounded revisioned editor
editor.purpose: The editor normalizes Unicode text, applies channel-specific caps and binds updates to the exact observed template revision.

actions.1: Review internal name, subject/title, body and a specific audit reason before confirmation.
actions.2: For SMS, watch the 160-character cost guidance; for push, keep the title near the recommended display length.

editor.guidance: The 160 SMS and 40-character push-title markers are guidance only. The enforced storage caps remain 1,600 and 80, and Core rejects rather than clamps an overlong value.

canonicalPreview.title: Canonical and draft preview
canonicalPreview.purpose: Stored Core-returned output is kept separate from the normalized browser draft so sanitization is never implied before Core performs it.

actions.1: For email, inspect stored canonical HTML in the no-network sandbox and inspect unsanitized draft only as inert source.
actions.2: For SMS and push, compare the safely rendered plain-text draft with the stored canonical item.

canonicalPreview.guidance: Only the closed canonical HTML tag/attribute vocabulary can enter the frame. Scripts, images, forms, active content and external requests remain impossible in the preview.

revisionReceipts.title: Revisions and durable receipts
revisionReceipts.purpose: Every create, update or delete persists a UUID, action, channel, target, expected revision and normalized material before the proxy call.

actions.1: When the pending banner appears, leave competing controls locked.
actions.2: Retry only the saved identity; accept exact replay, canonical success or authoritative conflict without minting a replacement request.

revisionReceipts.guidance: Timeout, lost response, in-progress, audit failure and uncertain write retain the same request. A different payload under the UUID is a terminal conflict.

deleteBoundary.title: Delete and delivery boundary
deleteBoundary.purpose: Deletion removes a template from future pickers at one exact revision and keeps a tombstone for replay/concurrency authority.

actions.1: Read the fresh confirmation naming the template, channel and revision.
actions.2: After success or conflict, adopt the returned tombstone or template instead of restoring or merging locally.

deleteBoundary.guidance: Deletion does not alter historical messages. This page has no recipient selector, campaign, delivery action, provider credential or delivery record.

profileLocation.title: Profile location limits help
profileLocation.summary: This page controls how far a member may move their public profile location from the browser location they explicitly shared. It sets policy radii, not anyone's exact position.

steps.1: Read the global radius and existing country exceptions before adding another rule.
steps.2: Use a country override only when product or safety policy genuinely differs for that country.
steps.3: Save or delete the exact rule and verify the refreshed active list.

globalPolicy.title: Global movement radius
globalPolicy.purpose: The global distance is the default limit whenever no active country-specific rule matches the member's country context.

actions.1: Review or update the bounded default distance.
actions.2: Use it as the baseline when evaluating every override.

globalPolicy.guidance: A tighter radius can block future profile-location changes. It does not reveal or rewrite stored exact coordinates.

countryOverride.title: Country-specific override
countryOverride.purpose: An override replaces the global radius for one ISO two-letter country code.

actions.1: Enter the canonical country code and the reviewed distance.
actions.2: Save a new rule or update the existing matching country rule.

countryOverride.guidance: Use the country code from the supported policy context, not a city name or a guessed location. Duplicates and invalid ranges are refused.

currentOverrides.title: Active country rules
currentOverrides.purpose: The list shows the country policies currently taking precedence over the global default.

actions.1: Review the effective radius for each country.
actions.2: Delete an override to return that country to the global default.

currentOverrides.guidance: Deletion removes the exception immediately; it does not delete member location data. Confirm the intended fallback before removing a rule.

datesActivities.title: Dates activities help
datesActivities.summary: Dates is the member-created activity area of Friending. This screen lets support and safety staff search every activity, understand its lifecycle and open a bounded operational detail without browsing raw database records.

steps.1: Search by a known activity, title, city or host and narrow the lifecycle or moderation state.
steps.2: Read host, timing, attendance and moderation columns together before opening a result.
steps.3: Use the detail page for any edit, command, sensitive location request or case investigation.

navigation.title: Dates workspace tabs
navigation.purpose: The tabs separate ordinary activity operations, the moderation queue and product configuration so operators do not mix content support with safety decisions or rollout controls.

actions.1: Stay on Activities for search and lifecycle support.
actions.2: Move to Moderation for reports and to Configuration for controlled catalogs or runtime policy.

navigation.guidance: The three areas use different capability levels. A visible read page does not imply permission to operate a case or change a setting.

filters.title: Primary activity filters
filters.purpose: Search, lifecycle, moderation, host and time filters reduce the server-paged inventory to the activity involved in a support or safety case.

actions.1: Use an exact activity ID when available; otherwise combine title, city or host with state filters.
actions.2: Apply the draft filters or reset them to restore the full bounded list.

filters.guidance: An empty filtered page proves only that no row matches those criteria. Reset before concluding that an activity is missing.

advancedFilters.title: Advanced ranges and sorting
advancedFilters.purpose: Optional ranges narrow attendance, reports, timestamps and other operational measurements, while sorting controls the review order.

actions.1: Expand advanced filters when a broad search still returns too many activities.
actions.2: Use minimum and maximum values consistently and select an order that matches the investigation.

advancedFilters.guidance: Ranges filter server projections; they are not editing limits. Clear both ends when a range is no longer relevant.

results.title: Activity results
results.purpose: Each row summarizes public identity, host, location label, schedule, lifecycle, moderation state and key counts before deeper access is granted.

actions.1: Compare the row with the reported activity and open the exact detail.
actions.2: Page through results without losing the applied filters.

results.guidance: List counts and labels are bounded support projections. Exact location, chat evidence and destructive commands remain behind separate controls.

datesConfiguration.title: Dates configuration help
datesConfiguration.summary: This page owns the bounded Dates capability and retention settings, member-visible activity types, and bilingual report reasons. Dates section availability is managed once on Configuration.

steps.1: Read the effective value and the dedicated runtime help before changing a feature, limit or retention rule.
steps.2: Keep stable catalog keys intact and update bilingual labels or active state with an audit reason.
steps.3: Refresh after a revisioned save and verify both the stored value and the effective product behavior.

runtimeSettings.title: Runtime settings
runtimeSettings.purpose: These allow-listed keys control rollout, lifecycle deadlines, capacity, abuse limits, moderation targets, retention and nearby digest behavior.

actions.1: Open the built-in Runtime settings help for the purpose, operational effect and caution attached to every key.
actions.2: Edit only the intended bounded value and save with its current revision.
actions.3: Compare stored and effective values, and use the separate Configuration control when the question is section availability.

runtimeSettings.guidance: Feature switches, workers and retention policy form one release unit. Never enable live location before positive retention and purge monitoring are proven.

activityTypes.title: Activity type catalog
activityTypes.purpose: Stable types provide the bilingual choices members use to describe an activity and determine their display order.

actions.1: Edit English and Hungarian labels, order and active state.
actions.2: Save against the current catalog revision.

activityTypes.guidance: Keys identify stored activities and must stay stable. Core refuses to disable the final active type so creation never receives an empty catalog.

reportReasons.title: Report reason catalog
reportReasons.purpose: Reasons give members consistent bilingual choices for reporting a user, activity, message or review, and assign the severity used by moderation.

actions.1: Filter reasons by scope and update labels, severity, entry points or active state.
actions.2: Add a new versioned reason when a genuinely new policy category is needed.

reportReasons.guidance: Reason IDs and keys preserve historical meaning. Deactivate obsolete choices instead of rewriting an old reason into a different policy concept.

datesModeration.title: Dates moderation queue help
datesModeration.summary: This is the safety queue for reports and prepublication cases associated with Dates. It exposes SLA, severity, assignment and redacted target context without opening sensitive evidence in the list.

steps.1: Choose the queue and status you are authorized to handle, then filter by assignment or an exact case identifier.
steps.2: Prioritize breached SLA, critical severity and escalated cases according to the moderation procedure.
steps.3: Open one case and claim its short reviewer lease before reading evidence or deciding it.

navigation.title: Dates workspace tabs
navigation.purpose: Navigation keeps moderation separate from general activity support and configuration work.

actions.1: Use Moderation for case handling.
actions.2: Return to Activities for non-case lifecycle support or Configuration for catalog policy.

navigation.guidance: Do not use an ordinary activity command as a substitute for a moderation decision when a safety case exists.

filters.title: Queue, status and assignee filters
filters.purpose: Filters narrow cases by queue, lifecycle state, assigned moderator and exact search terms while retaining the server-authored SLA view.

actions.1: Select your working queue and assignment, then apply.
actions.2: Reset filters when checking whether a case moved or closed.

filters.guidance: Reporter identities are intentionally redacted. Do not try to infer them from target or timing information.

caseQueue.title: Moderation cases
caseQueue.purpose: Rows summarize case ID, target, queue, severity, status, due time, report count, assignee and escalation state.

actions.1: Open the exact case that matches the task and SLA priority.
actions.2: Refresh after another moderator may have claimed or resolved it.

caseQueue.guidance: The list is not a decision surface. Evidence, conflicts of interest, legal holds and immutable resolution live in case detail.

datesModerationDetail.title: Dates moderation case help
datesModerationDetail.summary: This restricted workspace handles one Dates safety case from assignment through evidence review and immutable resolution. Capability, conflict-of-interest, revision and audit boundaries apply independently to every sensitive function.

steps.1: Confirm case target, severity, SLA and conflict state, then claim the five-minute lease.
steps.2: Read only the evidence necessary for the decision and add a concise internal note when it helps later reviewers.
steps.3: Choose the bounded resolution, confirm its user-facing effect and verify the immutable history entry.

overview.title: Case overview
overview.purpose: The overview provides redacted, server-authored queue state, target identity, severity, SLA, escalation and optimistic revision.

actions.1: Verify this is the intended case and inspect any conflict-of-interest block.
actions.2: Use the status badges to understand whether normal handling is still allowed.

overview.guidance: A detected conflict blocks ordinary evidence and decisions. Only an explicitly approved break-glass path may cross that boundary.

claim.title: Claim lease
claim.purpose: Claim, heartbeat and release coordinate active handling for a short five-minute window and reduce simultaneous moderation.

actions.1: Claim before adding notes, escalating or resolving.
actions.2: Keep the lease alive while working and release it if you stop.

claim.guidance: The lease does not freeze case facts. A stale optimistic revision still requires a full refresh.

reports.title: Reporter submissions
reports.purpose: This section collects the bounded member reports attached to the case while deliberately withholding reporter identity.

actions.1: Compare reason, text, timing and target across the submissions.
actions.2: Use distinct reports as corroborating context, not as an automatic verdict.

reports.guidance: Duplicate volume and reporter count do not replace policy review. Do not attempt to identify or contact a reporter from Webadmin.

evidence.title: Audited case evidence
evidence.purpose: Authorized evidence views provide the minimum activity, message, membership or location material retained for the case.

actions.1: Open only the evidence type needed for the current question.
actions.2: Supply the required reason for sensitive location access.

evidence.guidance: Every read is audited. Avoid copying sensitive evidence into notes, screenshots or external systems.

trailEvidence.title: Live-trail evidence capture
trailEvidence.purpose: This function copies one explicitly selected, bounded location window into restricted case evidence before the ordinary operational trail expires.

actions.1: Select only the necessary interval, within the two-hour and 1,000-point limits.
actions.2: State why the capture is necessary and confirm the audited operation.

trailEvidence.guidance: Capturing evidence does not stop normal trail purge and the audit must not contain coordinates. Use it only when location is material to the safety decision.

notesEscalation.title: Internal notes and escalation
notesEscalation.purpose: Notes preserve concise reviewer context; escalation raises the case to critical severity for senior attention.

actions.1: Add a factual, case-relevant internal note.
actions.2: Escalate when severity, uncertainty or procedure requires a higher-level review.

notesEscalation.guidance: Notes are restricted but durable. Do not include unnecessary personal data, speculation or copied evidence. Escalation is not a final decision.

resolution.title: Immutable resolution
resolution.purpose: Resolution records the bounded outcome, moderator reason and bilingual member-facing result and may change access or public content.

actions.1: Choose only an option valid for this target and case kind.
actions.2: Review the confirmation and user-visible consequence, then submit once.

resolution.guidance: A completed decision is immutable and audited. A stale or unsafe request is refused; refresh rather than selecting a different outcome to bypass it.

legalHold.title: Legal hold
legalHold.purpose: A legal hold suspends normal evidence-purge scheduling for material attached to this case until the hold is explicitly released.

actions.1: Place a hold only under the approved legal or safety procedure.
actions.2: Release it when the authority for extended retention ends.

legalHold.guidance: Legal hold is a high-impact retention action, not a convenient way to keep evidence for ordinary support.

history.title: Decision and appeal history
history.purpose: Append-only records show claims, notes, evidence operations, decisions, appeals, holds and other case lifecycle events.

actions.1: Verify the expected record after every sensitive operation.
actions.2: Use chronology to understand reopened or appealed cases without changing earlier facts.

history.guidance: Missing evidence of an operation is a reason to investigate, not to repeat an uncertain mutation immediately.

datesActivityDetail.title: Dates activity detail help
datesActivityDetail.summary: This page is the bounded operational record for one member-hosted Dates activity. It combines public state, support history, guarded edits, administrative commands, linked moderation and limited membership or chat summaries.

steps.1: Confirm activity ID, host, lifecycle, moderation state and current revision.
steps.2: Use a read-only section first; open sensitive location or a mutation only when the support case requires it.
steps.3: After an edit or command, verify the new revision, audit entry and expected lifecycle result.

overview.title: Activity overview
overview.purpose: The overview shows server-authored lifecycle, moderation, schedule, host, location label, join mode and attendance state.

actions.1: Confirm the record matches the reported activity.
actions.2: Read lifecycle and moderation badges together before using another section.

overview.guidance: A soft-deleted or terminal activity may remain visible for support history even though members can no longer operate it.

operationalHistory.title: Operational history summary
operationalHistory.purpose: Bounded counts and timestamps explain creation, publication, joins, reports, decisions and other retained activity milestones.

actions.1: Use the summary to build a timeline before reading deeper evidence.
actions.2: Compare counts with the detailed bounded lists below.

operationalHistory.guidance: Counts are support projections and may intentionally omit private content. They are not raw database totals.

publicFields.title: Edit public activity fields
publicFields.purpose: Authorized operators can correct the public title and details using the current optimistic revision.

actions.1: Change only the content required by the case and enter an audit reason.
actions.2: Save once and review the returned activity state.

publicFields.guidance: Editing an active public activity can send it back to prepublication moderation. Do not perform cosmetic rewrites unrelated to the request.

exactLocation.title: Exact location access
exactLocation.purpose: A separate guarded read can reveal sensitive exact-location data only when it is linked to an appropriate safety case.

actions.1: Provide the linked case and required reason.
actions.2: Read the location only for the authorized investigation.

exactLocation.guidance: The ordinary page intentionally shows only a location label. Exact access is audited and must never be used for routine member support.

commands.title: Lifecycle commands
commands.purpose: Bounded commands support safe administrative operations such as ending, canceling or soft-deleting when the current lifecycle permits them.

actions.1: Choose a command offered for the current state and enter a precise reason.
actions.2: Review the confirmation, then submit the revisioned request once.
