actions.1: Use a different approved owner for changes to your own active account.
actions.2: Confirm at least one valid owner path remains before removing another administrator.

ownerBoundary.guidance: A missing or disabled control is intentional protection. Do not bypass it through a lower-level Core call.

audit.title: Audit log help
audit.summary: The Audit log is the chronological, server-authored record of administrative mutations and sensitive operations. It identifies who acted, what operation ran, which target was involved and a deliberately safe subset of details.

steps.1: Refresh before investigating a recent change and start from the newest page.
steps.2: Match actor, action, target and timestamp to the operational event in question.
steps.3: Read safe details and withheld counts without expecting raw payloads or secrets.

navigation.title: Refresh and pagination
navigation.purpose: The page loads a bounded newest-first timeline and lets operators refresh or move through older server pages.

actions.1: Refresh after an expected operation to request the authoritative latest rows.
actions.2: Use Previous and Next to inspect older chronology without altering audit data.

navigation.guidance: The audit log is immutable from this screen and intentionally has no arbitrary browser-side query or delete control.

eventRows.title: Actor, action, target and time
eventRows.purpose: Each row anchors an administrative event to the authenticated email, stable action name, bounded target and server timestamp.

actions.1: Use the four fields together to distinguish similar repeated operations.
actions.2: Compare the event with the affected page's refreshed state or dedicated history.

eventRows.guidance: An audit row proves that Core recorded the operation, not that an external provider or client completed every downstream effect.

safeDetails.title: Safe detail projection
safeDetails.purpose: Only explicitly allow-listed scalar fields are rendered; nested, unknown, empty or overlong material is withheld and counted rather than exposed.

actions.1: Read the visible key-value pairs as bounded context.
actions.2: Note the withheld count when escalating through an authorized server-side investigation.

safeDetails.guidance: Withheld does not mean missing evidence. It protects secrets, private data and unbounded payloads from entering the browser or screenshots.

runtimeHelp.title: Runtime settings help
runtimeHelp.intro: This guide describes the Core-owned behavior behind every Dates runtime setting. It shows the value currently returned by Core, the stored value, the safe default and the validation bounds. Saving a value is immediate for new requests, but it does not migrate existing records or start background infrastructure.
runtimeHelp.beforeChangingCopy: Treat feature switches, retention rules and workers as one release unit. Use this order when enabling Dates or a high-impact capability:
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepRetention: Approve the privacy and legal retention values, especially live trails and moderation evidence.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepWorker: Deploy and verify the Dates background worker, monitoring and delivery dependencies.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepMaster: In Configuration, set Dates availability for the controlled storefronts and verify the client bootstrap and entry point.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepCapabilities: Enable creation, live sharing, reviews and digest separately; do not switch them all on at once.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepVerify: Watch errors, moderation queues, worker lag and audit logs before widening rollout.
runtimeHelp.effectiveNote: Dates section availability is edited in Configuration, not on this page. A subordinate effective value can still be OFF while its stored value is ON; the effective value is the operational witness.
runtimeHelp.timingNote: Durations and retention values are usually copied into a record when an activity, decline, case or purge schedule is created. Changing the default does not rewrite existing deadlines unless a dedicated migration or operation does so.
runtimeHelp.unknownCopy: Core returned settings that are not part of this Webadmin release's bounded help catalog.
runtimeHelp.unknownSettingCopy: Do not change this setting until the matching Core release notes and operating procedure have been reviewed.

dates_creation_enabled.title: Activity creation
dates_creation_enabled.purpose: Controls creation drafts and publishing of new Dates activities, including whether the app advertises the creation capability.
dates_creation_enabled.effect: ON permits eligible users to create and publish subject to validation, moderation and rate limits. OFF blocks the new-activity flow; existing activity data and allowed management operations remain available.
dates_creation_enabled.caution: Dates section availability is managed in Configuration. Disable creation first when stopping new supply while keeping existing activities operational.

dates_live_sharing_enabled.title: Host live-location sharing
dates_live_sharing_enabled.purpose: Controls the host's live session, pause/resume state and ingestion of bounded location trail points for an active activity.
dates_live_sharing_enabled.effect: ON permits live operations only when a positive live-trail retention is configured. OFF denies live session and point operations and exposes the capability as unavailable.
dates_live_sharing_enabled.caution: This handles highly sensitive location data. Set and approve dates_live_trail_retention_days, deploy the Dates worker and verify purge monitoring before enabling it.

dates_reviews_enabled.title: Post-activity reviews
dates_reviews_enabled.purpose: Controls participant review and host check-in capabilities after an activity ends, plus visibility of Dates review surfaces.
dates_reviews_enabled.effect: ON lets eligible participants submit/view the supported review flow. OFF fails review operations closed and removes the capability from the app; stored reviews and moderation history are not deleted.
dates_reviews_enabled.caution: Review moderation and evidence retention remain separate safety concerns. Dates section availability is managed in Configuration.

dates_digest_enabled.title: Nearby activity digest
dates_digest_enabled.purpose: Controls the background job that evaluates opted-in users and queues grouped nearby-activity suggestion notifications.
dates_digest_enabled.effect: ON lets the worker process eligible users according to frequency, quiet hours, origin and personal preferences. OFF makes digest batches exit without producing new digest events.
dates_digest_enabled.caution: This does not disable ordinary activity, reminder or moderation notifications. A running Dates worker and notification delivery path are required.

dates_default_scheduled_duration_minutes.title: Default scheduled duration
dates_default_scheduled_duration_minutes.purpose: The suggested activity length sent to clients when they build a new scheduled activity.
dates_default_scheduled_duration_minutes.effect: A larger value proposes a later end time; a smaller value proposes a shorter activity. It is a creation default, not the maximum duration enforced on every activity.
dates_default_scheduled_duration_minutes.caution: Existing drafts and activities are not rewritten. Clients normally pick up the new default after refreshing their Dates bootstrap.

dates_tbd_expiry_days.title: TBD activity lifetime
dates_tbd_expiry_days.purpose: Sets the automatic expiry deadline assigned to a newly created activity whose time is still to be decided.
dates_tbd_expiry_days.effect: After this many days the worker ends an unresolved TBD activity, invalidates pending membership states and makes its chat read-only. Longer values leave undecided activities discoverable longer.
dates_tbd_expiry_days.caution: The deadline is stored on creation and is not retroactively recalculated for existing TBD activities. Automatic expiry requires the Dates worker.

dates_now_lifetime_hours.title: Now activity lifetime
dates_now_lifetime_hours.purpose: Sets the automatic end deadline assigned when a new immediate, “Now” activity is created.
dates_now_lifetime_hours.effect: The worker ends the activity at its stored deadline, closes live sharing, invalidates pending membership states and makes chat read-only. A longer lifetime keeps immediate activities active longer.
dates_now_lifetime_hours.caution: Existing Now activities keep their stored auto-end time. This value does not replace manual host/admin end or cancel operations.

dates_now_warning_minutes.title: Now auto-close warning
dates_now_warning_minutes.purpose: Defines how far before a Now activity's auto-end deadline the system queues its one-time closing-soon warning.
dates_now_warning_minutes.effect: A larger value warns earlier; a smaller value warns closer to auto-close. The worker evaluates active activities against the current warning window.
dates_now_warning_minutes.caution: This changes notification timing only; it does not extend the activity lifetime. Worker cadence can affect the exact delivery minute.

dates_decline_cooldown_hours.title: Declined request cooldown
dates_decline_cooldown_hours.purpose: Prevents a user from immediately sending another join request after the host declines that user's request for the same activity.
dates_decline_cooldown_hours.effect: A decline writes a cooldown deadline using this value. Until that deadline, another join/request attempt is rejected. Larger values reduce repeat requests but also delay legitimate retries.
dates_decline_cooldown_hours.caution: Changing the setting affects cooldowns written by future declines; it does not rewrite an already stored cooldown_until value.

dates_invalidated_visibility_hours.title: Invalidated membership visibility
dates_invalidated_visibility_hours.purpose: Defines the short grace period during which an invitation or request invalidated by an activity ending, expiring or being canceled remains visible as historical state.
dates_invalidated_visibility_hours.effect: A larger value keeps the terminal state visible longer; a smaller value hides it sooner after invalidation. It supports understandable UI transitions without keeping it active.
dates_invalidated_visibility_hours.caution: This is a visibility deadline, not the retention policy for activity, chat, audit or moderation data. Existing stored deadlines are not globally rewritten.

dates_maximum_headcount_limit.title: Maximum selectable headcount
dates_maximum_headcount_limit.purpose: Caps the maximum_people value a host may choose for capacity-limited auto-join activities; the count includes the host.
dates_maximum_headcount_limit.effect: New or edited capacity values must be at least 2, no lower than the current going count and no higher than this limit. Approval-mode activities do not use this capacity field.
dates_maximum_headcount_limit.caution: Lowering the cap does not remove participants or automatically shrink existing activities, but a later edit must satisfy current validation.

dates_creation_rate_limit.title: Activity publish limit
dates_creation_rate_limit.purpose: Limits how many successfully published Dates activities one user can create in the preceding 24 hours.
dates_creation_rate_limit.effect: When the completed publish count reaches the limit, further publishes return a rate-limit error until earlier publishes leave the window. Draft editing is not itself a successful publish.
dates_creation_rate_limit.caution: Lowering the value does not unpublish activities. Set it high enough for legitimate hosts but low enough to contain spam and moderation load.

dates_request_rate_limit.title: Join-request attempt limit
dates_request_rate_limit.purpose: Limits repeated approval-mode join requests by one user for the same activity inside a 24-hour attempt window.
dates_request_rate_limit.effect: Each accepted request attempt increments the membership's request window counter. At the limit, another attempt is rejected until that window resets.
dates_request_rate_limit.caution: This works alongside the decline cooldown; it does not cap total requests received by a host across different users.

dates_rejoin_rate_limit.title: Rejoin attempt limit
dates_rejoin_rate_limit.purpose: Limits how often a user who left an auto-join activity can rejoin that same activity inside a 24-hour attempt window.
dates_rejoin_rate_limit.effect: The first join is not a rejoin. Subsequent left-to-joined transitions increment the per-membership rejoin counter and are rejected once the limit is reached.
dates_rejoin_rate_limit.caution: This protects membership and notification churn. It does not change host invitations, approval decisions or joins to other activities.

dates_chat_message_rate_limit.title: Chat messages per minute
dates_chat_message_rate_limit.purpose: Caps messages sent by one user to one Dates thread during the preceding 60 seconds, including supported update/pin messages.
dates_chat_message_rate_limit.effect: At the limit, another message to that thread returns a rate-limit error. Different senders and threads have independent counts.
dates_chat_message_rate_limit.caution: Raising this increases write, notification and abuse load. Lowering it does not delete or delay messages already accepted.

dates_live_point_rate_limit.title: Live location points per minute
dates_live_point_rate_limit.purpose: Caps newly accepted live-location trail points from one host across the preceding 60 seconds.
dates_live_point_rate_limit.effect: A batch is rejected when its new points plus the host's recent accepted points exceed the limit. Idempotent duplicate points do not consume the new-point count again.
dates_live_point_rate_limit.caution: Balance route quality against sensitive-data volume and write load. This setting matters only when live sharing and positive trail retention are both active.

dates_report_sla_hours.title: Report moderation SLA
dates_report_sla_hours.purpose: Sets the due-time target attached to new user-submitted Dates reports and their active moderation case.
dates_report_sla_hours.effect: The due timestamp is report creation time plus this many hours; a case keeps the earliest due time across attached reports. Queue SLA metrics and breach indicators use that timestamp.
dates_report_sla_hours.caution: Changing the value does not recalculate existing case deadlines, and it does not change the separate prepublication review deadline.

dates_distinct_report_suspend_threshold.title: Distinct-reporter escalation threshold
dates_distinct_report_suspend_threshold.purpose: Marks a report case as escalated when reports reach this number of unique reporter accounts.
dates_distinct_report_suspend_threshold.effect: At or above the threshold Core sets escalated=true so the case is more visible to moderators. Duplicate reports from the same reporter do not increase the distinct count.
dates_distinct_report_suspend_threshold.caution: Despite the historical key name, this does not automatically suspend an account or remove content. Restriction or suspension always requires an authorized moderation decision.

dates_activity_soft_delete_retention_day.title: Soft-deleted activity retention
dates_activity_soft_delete_retention_day.purpose: Sets the earliest hard-purge eligibility date when an administrator soft-deletes a Dates activity.
dates_activity_soft_delete_retention_day.effect: Soft delete immediately removes the activity from normal operation and writes purge_eligible_at for this many days later. Actual hard purge remains a separate authorized operation.
dates_activity_soft_delete_retention_day.caution: Changing the default does not reschedule already soft-deleted activities. Legal, audit, moderation and related-record constraints may require longer preservation.

dates_live_trail_retention_days.title: Live trail retention
dates_live_trail_retention_days.purpose: Defines how long terminated live-location sessions and point trails remain before worker-driven purge.
dates_live_trail_retention_days.effect: A positive day count enables safe live operations and supplies purge scheduling when an activity ends, is canceled or deleted. An empty value means unconfigured: live operations fail and the worker refuses unsafe processing.
dates_live_trail_retention_days.caution: This is a privacy-critical prerequisite for live sharing. Approve the period, run the Dates worker and monitor purge lag before turning live sharing ON; case evidence copied under authorization has its own policy.

moderation_evidence_retention_days.title: Moderation evidence retention
moderation_evidence_retention_days.purpose: Defines the post-hold retention period for restricted evidence snapshots stored with Dates moderation cases.
moderation_evidence_retention_days.effect: When an automatic or legal hold is closed, a positive value schedules evidence purge this many days later. An empty value does not create a new automatic purge deadline.
moderation_evidence_retention_days.caution: An active legal hold takes precedence. This setting does not purge case decisions or audit history and should be approved with privacy/legal owners before use.

dates_digest_frequency.title: Digest frequency
dates_digest_frequency.purpose: Selects the normal interval used by the Dates worker when rescheduling eligible nearby-activity digest evaluation.
dates_digest_frequency.effect: daily uses a one-day interval; weekly uses a seven-day interval. A digest is queued only when the user is eligible, opted in and has new joinable nearby activities.
dates_digest_frequency.caution: This is not a promise of an exact delivery time. Existing next-run timestamps, quiet hours, worker cadence and notification delivery can defer processing.

dates_digest_quiet_hours.title: Default digest quiet hours
dates_digest_quiet_hours.purpose: Provides the default local-time quiet-hour start and end advertised for Dates notification settings.
dates_digest_quiet_hours.effect: When quiet hours are enabled for a user, scheduled digest delivery is deferred while the user's local clock is inside this interval. A range such as 22:00–08:00 crosses midnight.
dates_digest_quiet_hours.caution: This is a default, not a mandatory global blackout. Existing explicit user preferences remain authoritative, and the user's timezone is used with UTC as a safe fallback.

hey.title: Hey
hey.summary: The product-wide gate above the Pinger rollout setting and the profile relation gesture.
hey.consequenceOff: Turning Hey off hides the Pinger button, the profile Hey gesture and the Heys collector tab, refuses new sends, and stops Hey bell rows and pushes. Existing Heys and matches remain; withdrawing a previous Hey stays possible.
hey.consequenceOn: Turning Hey on permits the relation gesture again. The Pinger button still appears only when its separate rollout configuration is enabled; nothing is reconstructed for the off period.

footprints.title: Footprints
footprints.summary: The product-wide gate for visits, Footprint badges and the entire Visits / Footprints / Likes collector.
footprints.consequenceOff: Turning Footprints off stops visit recording and Footprint badge sends, hides the whole collector and stops Footprint alerts and pushes. Existing records remain. The photo-like gesture on profile media still works and still notifies its owner; only its collector tab disappears.
footprints.consequenceOn: Turning Footprints on resumes new visits, badge sends and the collector from now on. Nothing is reconstructed for the off period, and existing records become reachable again.
